question: An exam asks about overfitting and the train-test split. Which answer should receive full credit?
options: Overfitting is memorization that fails on new data.
Testing on training data validates a model.
More complex models always generalize better.
gold_answer: Overfitting is memorization that fails on new data.
notes: Team-authored original item on overfitting and the train-test split. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Testing on training data validates a model.

claims.text: A held-out test set estimates fresh-data performance.

evidence.text: Because the model never trained on it, held-out data mimics unseen future inputs.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes held-out data mimicking unseen inputs, which entails the claim.

evidence.text: Well-tuned regularization trades small training loss for better fresh-data accuracy.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes accuracy gains from regularization, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Machine learning eliminates the need for data collection.

evidence.text: Data budgets were discussed for the proposed project.

claims.verdict_rationale: Discussing budgets cannot settle the claim, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Overfitting is memorization that fails on new data.

claims.text: Validation data should guide model selection, not final reporting.

evidence.text: Tuning on validation leaks information into choices, so final claims need untouched test data.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage requires untouched data for final claims, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Zero training error guarantees deployment success.

evidence.text: Memorized training sets give zero error while fresh-data error stays high, the hallmark of overfitting.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage pairs zero training error with high fresh error, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Dataset-model fit was assessed for the candidate approaches.

claims.verdict_rationale: Assessing fit cannot show every dataset fits any model, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

claims.text: Overfit models fit noise in the training data.

evidence.text: Excess capacity encodes sampling quirks that do not repeat in fresh data.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes encoding non-repeating quirks, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Test data may be used for training when convenient.

evidence.text: Training on the test set destroys its role as an unbiased judge of generalization.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states training destroys the test role, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Human review is obsolete after automation.

evidence.text: Review workloads were tracked before and after tool deployment.

claims.verdict_rationale: Tracking workloads cannot show review is obsolete, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
